title: Islanded Reserve Orchestration: tenant-level reserve profiles, staged autoscale, and controlled burst rebalancing (PRD)
creator: Priya Shah
description: Summary: Define and deliver 'Islanded Reserve Orchestration' — a reserved-capacity feature that lets tenants own logical reserve profiles (islands) with staged autoscale behavior and controlled burst rebalancing across zones. Purpose is to improve latency stability for reserved customers during noisy neighbor events while enabling predictable bursting and graceful degradation.
problem_statement: Reserved capacity customers sometimes experience latency spikes and unpredictable preemption during large cross-tenant bursts. Current reserved pools are coarse-grained, which forces either over-provisioning or frequent manual intervention. We need a mechanism to provide tenant-isolated reserve profiles with configurable autoscale stages and safe, policy-driven burst rebalancing so that reserved customers retain predictable latency and operators can recover capacity without customer impact.
goals: Provide tenant-scoped reserve profiles (islands) that guarantee an inner reservation and an elastic outer band for burst activity
Implement staged autoscale policies (steady, warm, burst) with configurable thresholds and cooldowns
Add a controlled burst-rebalancing engine that can reclaim or re-route ephemeral capacity with safety checks and telemetry
Expose policy primitives in the Console and API for self-serve configuration
Ensure minimal end-user request latency regression at 99th percentile compared to current reserved pools
non_goals: Replace multi-tenant billing model — billing changes will be scoped separately
Implement fully automated cross-region warmup (out of scope for initial rollout)
Support on-prem private deployments in v1 (later iteration only)
user_stories: As a platform engineer, I want to assign a tenant to a reserve island with a base reservation and burst band so critical apps don't suffer during tenant churn
As an SRE, I want autoscale stages to move capacity from warm to burst only after defined latency thresholds are breached
As a product owner, I want to configure a burst rebalancing policy that prefers reclaimed preemptible capacity before evicting steady reservations
As a customer, I want the Console to show my island's headroom and recent rebalancing events so I can audit behavior
functional_requirements: FR-1: Create Reserve Island entity: id, tenant_id, base_reservation_gpus, burst_band_gpus, warm_headroom, zone_affinity
FR-2: Staged autoscaler: states {steady,warm,burst} with configurable thresholds (p95 latency, queue depth, token rate) and cooldown windows
FR-3: Burst rebalancer: policy engine that executes preemption hierarchy (ephemeral -> preemptible -> soft-evict steady) and supports dry-run and force modes
FR-4: API: CRUD for island profiles, autoscale policies, and manual rebalancing triggers with RBAC controls
FR-5: Telemetry: streaming events for state transitions, rebalancing actions, rejection reasons, and per-tenant p50/p95/p99 latency during transitions
FR-6: SLO safety: automatic fallback to a designated compatible model variant when steady capacity is insufficient
console_ui_changes: Add a Reserve Islands page under Dedicated > Capacity showing list of islands, reservation/burst metrics, a policy editor modal, and a timeline of rebalancing events. In the per-tenant Capacity view add a badge linking to its island with quick actions: scale-up, scale-down, and open dry-run rebalancing.
api_spec: POST /v1/dedicated/islands -> create island; GET /v1/dedicated/islands/{id} -> retrieve; PATCH /v1/dedicated/islands/{id} -> update policies; POST /v1/dedicated/islands/{id}/rebalance?mode={dry_run|execute} -> trigger rebalancer; authentication via tenant-scoped API keys; actions constrained by entitlements.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: An operator can create an island with base_reservation and burst_band via API and see the entity in Console within 30s
AC-2: Staged autoscaler transitions between steady->warm->burst based on configured thresholds and emits events to telemetry within 10s of state change
AC-3: Burst rebalancer honors policy hierarchy and during a controlled test reclaims preemptible capacity before impacting base_reservation for at least 95% of simulated burst patterns
AC-4: Per-tenant p99 latency during a simulated 10x burst remains <= 1.25x of baseline for customers with base_reservation >= 2 cards
AC-5: Dry-run rebalancing provides deterministic action list in Console and API without modifying actual allocations
AC-6: RBAC prevents non-admins from executing forced rebalances; IAM roles map to Console permissions
AC-7: Release includes end-to-end integration tests and a runbook for operators; runbook validated in two on-call drills
success_metrics: SM-1: 99th percentile latency for reserved customers during cross-tenant bursts reduced by 30% compared to baseline
SM-2: Number of manual interventions to rebalance reserved pools reduced by 70% in the first 90 days
SM-3: Percentage of reclaim actions that avoid evicting steady reservations >= 95%
SM-4: Time-to-create and apply island policy in Console < 60s for 95% of users
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal alpha): limited tenants + SRE test harness; Phase 2 (private beta): selected paid customers, limited zones; Phase 3 (general availability): public for Dedicated customers with opt-in for existing reservations. Each phase gated by telemetry targets and two successful on-call drills. Feature flag for rebalancer control and dry-run default enabled at GA rollout.
monitoring_and_alerting: Add dashboards: Island health, autoscaler transitions, rebalancer action rate, per-tenant latency deltas. Alerts: >5% unexpected steady eviction rate in 1h, autoscaler flapping > 6 transitions in 10m, dry-run mismatch rate >10% when compared to executed runs.
risks: R1: Incorrect thresholds could cause oscillation (flapping) — mitigated via cooldowns and manual override
R2: Rebalancer logic may incorrectly evict steady capacity under rare spike patterns — mitigate with staged rollout and dry-run validation
R3: Console complexity may overwhelm customers — mitigate with presets and guided defaults
R4: Billing/entitlement edge cases when islands span reservation tiers — coordinate with Finance
notes: This PRD intentionally separates policy primitives from billing. Implementation should prioritize safety (dry-run first) and developer ergonomics. Early beta customers will include two latency-sensitive SaaS partners identified by AE. Align with security for IAM scoping before private beta. Consider follow-up to support cross-region warmup and on-prem packaging.
